name: the grid applies to a collapsed cell too
why: The tile grid is for an EXPANDED cell; on a collapsed one the grid's fixed columns would widen every row of the table. The :has() condition is what keeps it to expanded cells.
grep: grid is the default

name: the image card is not hooked on the image
why: B2 is shown by the delegated tooltip engine from the li's data-mbtt-fn; without it there is no card at all (and, the card replacing them, no preview either).
grep: B2: hovering an image

name: the image card shows plain pills, not the cell's marked ones
why: The card copies the cell's own pill nodes so they carry the filter highlight; rebuilding them from text loses the "Medi" mark.
grep: B2: hovering an image

name: the release card is not hooked on the icon and count
why: B1 rides on data-mbtt-fn=art-sum stamped by _artDecorateArtCell(); without it the icon keeps its plain "16 images" tooltip.
grep: B1: the icon shows

name: chip letters are text
why: The letters must be CSS content: as text they reach the filter text, so a typed "Bk" would match every release.
grep: chips: filled, hollow

name: EAA cells take the CAA chip vocabulary
why: The chip types come from the cell's ctx; an EAA cell must show Poster/Banner/…, not Front/Back/….
grep: EAA cells use the EAA chip vocabulary

name: the grouped layout does not stamp group headers
why: Without the per-image group data, grouped is just the grid: no headers, archive order.
grep: the layout is CSS only

name: ← → at the end of a row wrap instead of crossing rows
why: Opened from the column, → on the last image must go on to the next visible row (sa_art_viewer_cross_rows).
grep: D1: a click opens the viewer

name: Shift+← → step images instead of rows
why: Shift+arrows must change rows; without the branch they fall through to the plain step.
grep: steps the VISIBLE rows

name: the column click listens on the document, after the navigation guard
why: initNavigationGuard()'s anchor guard is a document capture listener registered first; a document listener of ours runs after it, so a plain icon click asks "leave the page?" instead of opening the viewer.
grep: a plain icon click is the viewer's

name: a Ctrl-click on the icon opens the viewer too
why: Any modifier must leave the link to the browser.

if (e.button !== 0 || e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey || e.shiftKey || e.altKey) return;

name: an older record is loaded at its 500 px large size
why: Records without a 1200 key still have the 1200 px file (probe-caa-thumbnail-keys.py); the viewer must ask for it.
grep: an older record without a 1200 key

name: no fallback when the 1200 px file fails
why: A failed 1200 must fall back to the 500 px large, not leave the thumbnail with an error note.

edits.find: return urls.reduce((p, u) => p.catch(() => _artViewerLoad(u)), Promise.reject(new Error('no url')));

grep: an older record without a 1200 key

name: a step resets the zoom although it should be kept
why: With sa_art_viewer_remember_zoom on (the default) the zoom stays from image to image.
grep: zooms and the zoom is kept

name: the artwork findings are never re-stamped
why: stampFindings() runs before the artwork arrives; only the per-row re-stamp can count the two artwork findings.
grep: findings: no Front / no Medium

name: a release without artwork counts as no Front image
why: Defensive today, and recorded as such: a release whose record is empty never builds a multi-row cell, so _artQueueFindingsRestamp() never queues its row, and stampFindings() runs before any record (session or IDB) is read — a second press reloads the page. The guard is what keeps a later full stamp (should one ever run with the cache filled) from flagging releases without artwork, which the 2026-10-06 decision excludes.
grep: findings: no Front / no Medium

name: a digital release counts as missing a Medium image
why: "No Medium image" only applies to physical formats; Digital Media is skipped.
grep: findings: no Front / no Medium

name: a tap on a tile does not open the viewer
why: On a phone the tile tap is the only way in (no hover).
grep: a tap on a tile opens the viewer

name: the CAA column gets no ▶N▤ proxy
why: initCollapsableColumns() places none on an art column; without the art code's proxy the multi-row count and its handle are gone (reported 2026-10-06).
grep: is there from the first render

name: a ▶N▤ proxy click is not forwarded to the ▶🖼 button
why: The proxy is a second handle on the ▶🖼 button's ▶; without the forward a click does nothing.
grep: is there from the first render

name: the ▶N▤ proxy does not follow the ▶🖼 button
why: Toggled from the ▶🖼 button, the proxy must show the same state.
grep: is there from the first render

name: the summary line neither wraps nor keeps its wrapper's width
why: Next to the type chips the prose wrapper div shrank to the icon's width and the cache hint + count dropped below the icon (debug/MGV-CAA-bug.html). Either rule alone cures it (flex-wrap moves the chips down before anything shrinks), so the defect is both gone.
